Chronic lymphocytic leukemia commonly manifests insidiously with fatigue and weight loss due to marrow infiltration and immune dysregulation; it is under-recognized in initial evaluation of constitutional symptoms. Tuberculosis (especially extrapulmonary or miliary) remains a key infectious mimic in endemic areas or immunocompromised hosts, causing profound catabolism and weakness without classic pulmonary symptoms. Adrenal insufficiency fits the profile of progressive fatigue and weight loss, and while cold intolerance was asked about (but not confirmed), its absence doesn’t rule it out—only ~50% of patients report it early, and hyponatremia or postural hypotension would be more specific clues pending further assessment. Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is top-ranked due to its classic presentation with insidious fatigue, weight loss, and frequent occult night sweats (not yet confirmed but highly prevalent); it commonly lacks early focal signs, aligning with the sparse positive findings so far. Crohn’s disease follows closely: weight loss and weakness are common in active disease, and it may present without overt diarrhea or blood initially—especially in upper GI or ileal-predominant forms; mouth ulcers (not yet endorsed) would further support this. Chronic myeloid leukemia fits the chronicity, constitutional symptoms, and fatigue from cytopenias or splenomegaly, though it typically presents with more hematologic clues (e.g., early satiety, left upper quadrant discomfort). Pulmonary TB is included given weight loss and fatigue as cardinal features—even without cough or fever yet—and remains endemic in many populations; night sweats would strongly reinforce this. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is ranked fifth: weight loss and weakness are nearly universal at diagnosis, often preceding pain or jaundice by months; however, it usually progresses more rapidly than described, and absence of steatorrhea or new-onset diabetes reduces likelihood. All other broad categories (e.g., depression, hypothyroidism, COPD) were excluded due to lack of supporting features in the limited interrogation and lower specificity for isolated weight loss + weakness without fatigue modifiers (e.g., cold intolerance, exertional dyspnea). Diagnostic uncertainty remains moderate due to symptom non-specificity and absence of key discriminating questions (e.g., fever, lymphadenopathy, abdominal pain, stool frequency, respiratory symptoms)."}
